claude_only.name: Which system generated the message's primary identifier and what is its uniqueness guarantee and scope?
Is identity single-valued or composite, and if composite which attributes form the key?
Which secondary identifiers exist for this message and who assigned each one?
Does each recipient copy carry the same identifier, and how is a copy distinguished from the original record?
Which classification axes apply to this message and which are mandatory for the channel?
What urgency or priority is asserted, by whom, and does it change handling or retention?
What sensitivity or confidentiality label applies and what handling constraint does it impose?
How is the human-readable subject distinguished from the machine-resolvable topic or about-reference?
What is the ordered part tree of this message and what is the structural role of each node?
What media type, subtype, parameters and transfer encoding are declared for each part, and were they verified against the octets?
Which part is the canonical representation when several alternatives express the same content?
What natural language and character encoding apply to each textual part?
Is each payload carried by value or by reference, and if by reference what resolves the reference and for how long?
For structured payloads, which schema governs the data and how is schema identity conveyed?
What digest or checksum binds the payload to this message, and over what canonical octets was it computed?
Who owns the carried object and does carriage transfer any rights or obligations?
Who authored the message and who actually released it, and are they the same party?
If the message was sent on behalf of another party, what authorises that and is the authorisation still valid at send time?
Where should replies and where should failure reports be directed, and why do they differ?
Is the originator identity fully disclosed as required for the message purpose and jurisdiction?
What addressing role does each recipient entry carry and is that role visible to other recipients?
Which addressing variant does this stored copy represent — originator view, recipient view or redistributed view?
Which addressing fields must be removed or masked before this message is forwarded, archived or exported?
When the target is a topic, room or audience rather than a named party, how is the addressed set determined and bounded?
What address did the sender submit for this recipient and what address actually received the message?
Did this recipient entry expand into multiple targets, and is the resulting set knowable to the sender?
Was the message redirected or forwarded after acceptance, and does downstream evidence still correlate to the original entry?
Does a permission or suppression decision taken on the submitted address still hold for the resolved address?
What are the envelope originator and envelope recipients, and how do they differ from the header-declared parties?
Which of the two identifier sets was authenticated, and by which mechanism?
Is envelope data retained after delivery, and under what rule may it be erased?
For non-mail channels, which construct plays the envelope role and what is its retention behaviour?
What is the ordered sequence of handling agents and what did each one assert about time and origin?
What guarantees that trace entries were not altered or reordered after the fact?
Which trace entries were created inside the trust boundary of the recording organisation and which are untrusted assertions?
When must trace and traffic data be erased or anonymised, and what is the lawful basis for retaining it longer?
Is the thread identifier channel-assigned or derived by reconstruction, and by which algorithm?
What determines whether a message belongs to the thread, and can membership change after the fact?
Who participates in the thread, and does a participant see the whole thread or only the messages addressed to them?
How are thread splits, merges and subthreads represented without breaking existing references?
Which message does this one reply to, and is that parent resolvable in the current holding?
What ancestor chain is asserted, and does it agree with the parent pointer and the thread assignment?
How is a broken, forged or circular reference chain detected and represented?
Does the reply quote or transclude the parent content, and does that create a second copy under separate custody?
What kind of derivation produced this message: forward, resend, correction, replacement or recall?
Who is accountable for the redistributed message, and does original authorship survive the derivation?
Was the original content preserved unaltered, and how is any alteration recorded?
Does the channel support withdrawal of an already-released message, and what does withdrawal actually guarantee?
What correlation token binds this response to its request, and who minted it?
Where should the response be sent, and is that target different from the request's reply address?
Is a response required, optional or forbidden, and what happens if none arrives within the expected window?
Does this message fulfil a prior request or order, and is that fulfilment complete or partial?
At which level is state asserted — the whole message, one recipient entry, or one delivery attempt?
Which states are terminal, which are retryable, and what distinguishes a permanent from a transient failure?
Which state transitions are permitted and which agent role may assert each transition?
How is a message recorded as entered in error or never actually sent, without deleting the record?
Which distinct time points are recorded for this message and what does each one actually mean?
Is event time separated from observation or ingestion time, and which one is authoritative for ordering?
Whose clock produced each timestamp and what is known about its trustworthiness or synchronisation?
Is the sender's local offset known, and how is an unknown offset represented rather than guessed?
Does the message expire, and what happens to it and to its evidence at expiry?
Which agent issued the status record and was it authorised to speak for the delivery attempt?
What outcome code was reported, from which registry, and how does it map to the model's outcome classifier?
How does the status record correlate back to the original message and to a specific recipient entry?
Can multiple, later or contradictory status records exist for the same recipient, and which one prevails?
Which named evidence event does this record attest, and at which point of the transfer?
Who issued the evidence, under which issuing policy, and is that issuer a qualified provider?
What legal presumption, if any, does this evidence carry and in which jurisdiction?
How is the evidence cryptographically bound to the exact payload it attests?
How long must the evidence remain verifiable, and what preserves its validity beyond signature expiry?
What delivery guarantee did the channel provide for this message, and who selected it?
How is a duplicate delivery detected and what is the idempotency key?
What may be concluded from the absence of an acknowledgement under this guarantee level?
Does the channel retain the message for later subscribers or offline recipients, and for how long?
What disposition is reported, and does it mean the content was actually presented to a person?
Did the sender request a disposition notification, and did the recipient consent to sending one?
What is the evidential weight of this report and which specific claims may not be made from it?
What does a disposition report disclose about the recipient, and is that disclosure permissible?
How is the notification target validated to prevent amplification or mail-bombing abuse?
Which authentication methods were evaluated, against which identifier, with what result?
Which authentication service stamped the result and is it inside the consuming organisation's trust boundary?
How are forged or externally injected authentication assertions detected and removed?
What downstream decision may be based on the result, and what must not be inferred from a pass?
Which parts of the message are confidentiality-protected and which metadata remains observable to intermediaries?
Can integrity still be verified from the stored form, and what canonicalisation is required to do so?
Which storage or transport transformations would invalidate the integrity evidence, and are they prohibited?
If content is end-to-end protected, what remains discoverable, auditable or retainable by the custodian?
On what basis was this recipient contacted for this purpose on this channel?
When was the permission state evaluated relative to release, and was a fresher state available?
Does the basis cover this purpose and this resolved address, or only the address originally submitted?
What would be produced to demonstrate the permission if challenged, and where is it held?
Does the message carry a valid, working cessation mechanism appropriate to its purpose and channel?
Are the opt-out headers covered by the message's authentication signature so a receiver may act on them?
When an opt-out is exercised, what scope does it suppress and within what deadline must it take effect?
How does a suppression signal interact with a still-valid permission record or a non-marketing message?
What retention rule applies to this message, at what granularity, and who assigned it?
Do content, addressing metadata, traffic data and evidence share one retention period or different ones?
What event starts the retention clock and what event ends it?
What suspends disposition, who may impose and lift that suspension, and how is it evidenced?
Which fields are removed by a redaction and which are deliberately preserved, and why?
Which copies does a deletion or redaction actually reach, and which remain beyond the actor's control?
What tombstone or audit evidence remains after destruction, and is it sufficient to prove lawful disposal?
How does redaction interact with signatures, digests and delivery evidence over the redacted content?
Which custodians hold a copy of this message and how does each copy differ from the originator's?
Who may read each copy by default, and which role grants exceptions?
Under what authority may a message be disclosed to a third party, and what is recorded about the disclosure?
What access and disclosure events must be audited, and how long is the audit trail itself kept?
When the message contains personal data about a third party, how are their rights handled without breaching the correspondents' confidentiality?

grok_only.name: What is the authoritative origin identifier of this message, which system issued it, and under which scheme?
Is there a submission or envelope transaction identifier distinct from the content identifier, and must it be preserved for delivery reports?
Is this communication intentionally transient, and if so may a global identifier be omitted?
What local store key does this Dimension assign, and how does it reference the origin identifier?
Who authored this message and, if different, which agent transmitted it?
When was the message completed, when was it sent, and when was this copy ingested, each as RFC 3339 with offset or Z?
What is the current lifecycle status and status reason, including rare states such as preparation, not-done, entered-in-error or deleted?
Where should replies be directed if Reply-To or equivalent is present?
What is the ordered tree of content parts, and which media type and transfer encoding applies to each?
What language tags or language maps apply to subject, summary and body, and is any language undetermined?
If rendered content was derived from another markup, what is the source media type and source text identifier?
If transfer encoding is unrecognized, must the part be treated as application/octet-stream regardless of declared Content-Type?
Which documents or blobs does this message carry or point to, and is each inline, attached or reference-only?
What digest was computed over the conveyed octets, with which algorithm, and did it match at ingest?
Do HTML or other parts reference sibling parts by Content-ID, and are those parts present?
Which parent and ancestor message identifiers does this message claim, and do they resolve in this store?
What thread identifier and topic group this message, and when did the thread start?
Is this a reply, a resend/reintroduction, a forward, or an in-response-to clinical follow-up?
Must this server forward the activity to collections it owns because the origin could not expand them?
Who are the primary, copy and blind-copy recipients on this copy of the message, and which collections were targeted?
Was Bcc/bcc/bto stripped before this copy was transmitted, and must this copy omit other Bcc identities?
Is the message addressed to the public collection or equivalent, and must it remain readable without authentication?
Which channel type and provider actually carried this message, and was the hop an origin, relay, gateway or delivery system?
If federated social transport, which outbox accepted the activity and which inbox or sharedInbox was posted?
If a clinical communication, what medium codes describe how information was shared?
What is the endpoint value and scheme, and which agent owns it?
Has this endpoint been verified, when, by whom, and using what method?
Must local-part case and exact spelling be preserved, and is the domain an FQDN?
What reverse-path and forward-paths were on the envelope, and how do they differ from header addresses?
When did this hop accept responsibility, and is it obligated to deliver or emit a failure report?
What ordered trace hops exist, and were they prepended without reordering?
Is the reverse-path null to suppress further status notifications?
For each envelope recipient, what DSN action and status code were reported, and is that state terminal?
If delayed, when was the last attempt and until when will retries continue?
Was successful submission to a mailing-list exploder treated as final delivery, or was an alias expanded with a non-terminal expanded action?
Did a gateway translate a foreign non-delivery notice, and which DSN-Gateway and foreign address-type apply?
Was an MDN requested, does Disposition-Notification-To match Return-Path, and has the user consented to send one?
What disposition occurred, in which mode, at what time, and which UA reported it?
If displayed, is there any claim that the content was understood, and is that claim disallowed by the MDN semantics?
Does this channel support recall or delete-propagation, and was a recall requested or completed?
If deleted, is a Tombstone retained, with which deleted timestamp, and what HTTP semantics should a fetch return?
Has the originator blocked an actor, and must delivery of the Block activity to that actor be suppressed?
For this subject, channel and purpose, is contact permitted, on which lawful basis, and where is the demonstration evidence?
Has consent been withdrawn, when, through which channel, and was withdrawal as easy as grant?
Has the recipient consented to emit MDNs globally or per message, and is the default still suppress?
Has the subject blocked the sender or objected to this category of contact?
Who owns this stored copy, and is it the origin, a recipient inbox, a Bcc copy or an archive hold?
Which redaction profile applies, and which fields are omitted from this view?
If no authorization is presented, which messages if any are visible?
Until when must this communication record, its receipts and its consent evidence be retained, and under which class?
Is a legal or clinical hold active, who placed it, and does it override erasure?
Has erasure been requested, what was done to origin and copies, and were federated copies only tombstoned locally?
What digest identifies this stored copy, over which canonicalization, and when was it computed?
Was the object dereferenced at its origin identifier and did it match, or was it accepted as transient?
What authentication or signature results accompany this copy, and are they informational only?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
